newsitem.title: JAPAN: Wakashio Bank reveals problem loans as of end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Wakashio Bank reveals problem loans as of end-Sept.

text.p: Wakashio Bank, set up earlier this year to take over the assets of failed Taiheiyo Bank Ltd, said on Monday that it had bad loans worth 1.28 billion yen to bankrupt firms as of the end of September.
Wakashio said in a statement that it also had 11.79 billion yen worth of non-performing loans with interest payments in arrears by six months or more.

The bank said it posted a current parent profit of 229 million yen for the six-month period to September 31, but marked a net loss of 1.68 billion yen. Its half-year operating profit totalled 300 million yen.

The bank said it expects a current profit of 300 million yen and an operating profit of 900 million yen for the full year to March 31, 1997. It forecast a net loss of 1.8 billion yen for the full year.
Taiheiyo Bank Ltd was a regional bank that failed in March due to huge bad loans. It was only the second Japanese bank failure in more than 50 years.
